classification.classification_note: The reproduced fault is a 1-byte write past the stack `lookupname[128]` buffer in the no-runtime-IDNA punycode fallback. The source-level defect is the missing reservation for the trailing NUL before the last label's ACE payload is encoded.

bug_description.normalized: The staged `poc` is a single 62-byte UTF-8 PSL rule with 11 dot-separated labels: `ڸoa`, `Dڸ88`, `ڸoa`, `ڸ88`, `Dڸo8`, `ڸoa`, `Dڸ88`, `Dڸ888`, `Dڸ`, `Dڸo88`, `Dڸo88`. `psl_load_fp()` reads that line as one text suffix rule, `suffix_init()` copies it into `suffix.label_buf`, and `add_punycode_if_needed()` takes the non-ASCII path. In the staged build, `psl_idna_toASCII()` executes the fallback branch with stack `lookupname[128]` and calls `domain_to_punycode()`. Using the in-tree punycode encoder, the first 10 labels plus their dots consume 116 bytes of that buffer. The final label `Dڸo88` has UTF-8 length 6, so the vulnerable pre-check `outlen + labellen + (e != NULL) + 4 >= outsize` still passes at `116 + 6 + 0 + 4 = 126`. After copying the `xn--` prefix, line 595 sets `labellen = outsize - outlen`, i.e. `8`, instead of reserving one byte for the trailing terminator. `punycode_encode()` then fills those last 8 bytes with `Do88-qrg`, making `outlen == 128`, and line 604 writes `out[outlen] = 0` one byte past `lookupname[128]`. Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1` in `domain_to_punycode -> psl_idna_toASCII -> add_punycode_if_needed -> psl_load_fp`. The staged patch fixes the witness-specific obligation by changing that length assignment to `outsize - outlen - 1`.

evidence_note: The saved sanitizer trace localizes the crash to `domain_to_punycode` at `src/psl.c:604` and shows the enclosing `psl_idna_toASCII` frame contains stack object `lookupname` from line 788 with valid range `[1184, 1312)`. The faulting write hits offset 1312 exactly, and the same frame also exposes inlined `input` from `domain_to_punycode` line 568, which matches the patched fallback punycode path.

source.description: First project-code read of attacker-controlled PSL text on the vulnerable path.
source.value_from: The staged witness `gt_results/arvo_38985/poc` is exactly 62 bytes with no trailing newline: `da b8 6f 61 2e 44 da b8 38 38 2e da b8 6f 61 2e da b8 38 38 2e 44 da b8 6f 38 2e da b8 6f 61 2e 44 da b8 38 38 2e 44 da b8 38 38 38 2e 44 da b8 2e 44 da b8 6f 38 38 2e 44 da b8 6f 38 38`, decoded as `ڸoa.Dڸ88.ڸoa.ڸ88.Dڸo8.ڸoa.Dڸ88.Dڸ888.Dڸ.Dڸo88.Dڸo88`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: The raw input line is first materialized here as the concrete domain string and label count that drive the later punycode conversion.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: For the witness line, `suffix_init()` copies the full 62-byte rule into `suffix->label_buf` and counts 11 dot-separated labels, preserving the final label `Dڸo88` that triggers the exact-fill condition.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The non-ASCII label path gives `punycode_encode()` all remaining buffer bytes after the `xn--` prefix instead of reserving one byte for the trailing NUL.
root_cause.note: On the witness's final label, `outlen` is already 120 after the prefix copy, so this statement sets `labellen = 8` and allows the ACE tail to occupy bytes 120..127. The fix changes this exact line to `outsize - outlen - 1`.

sink.description: Sink. After the final punycode label exactly fills `lookupname[128]`, this terminator write lands at index 128, one byte past the stack buffer.
sink.note: Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1` at `src/psl.c:604:15` in `domain_to_punycode`, and the enclosing `psl_idna_toASCII` frame identifies `lookupname` line 788 as the overflowed object.

parser_admitted.description: The witness is admitted as a text PSL rule and reaches punycode augmentation.
parser_admitted.note: The first line is 62 bytes long, so `is_dafsa` at line 1202 is false, the line is neither whitespace nor comment, and `suffix_init()` accepts it because `62 < sizeof(label_buf) - 1`. Control then reaches `add_punycode_if_needed(idna, psl->suffixes, suffixp)` at line 1315.

fine_trace.note: Source. `psl_load_fp()` reads the attacker-controlled PoC bytes into `buf` as the first line of a text PSL file. For this witness, that line is the entire 62-byte UTF-8 rule `ڸoa.Dڸ88.ڸoa.ڸ88.Dڸo8.ڸoa.Dڸ88.Dڸ888.Dڸ.Dڸo88.Dڸo88`.

The loader materializes the rule into parser state here. The copied string is still 62 bytes long and contains 11 labels, so the later per-label punycode loop will eventually process final label `Dڸo88` with ten already-emitted predecessors.
The copied rule is not pure ASCII because every label contains UTF-8 bytes `da b8` for `ڸ`, so the early return is skipped and the rule enters punycode conversion.

The staged build executes the fallback branch with a fixed 128-byte stack destination. The saved ASan frame reports this exact `lookupname` object as the overflowed buffer, so every later `outlen` calculation is bounded by 128 bytes.

Before the crashing iteration, the first 10 labels are emitted successfully into `lookupname`. Using the in-tree punycode encoder, those 10 ACE labels plus their 10 dots occupy 116 bytes, so the final label starts with only 12 buffer bytes left.

For the last label `Dڸo88`, `mem_is_ascii(label, labellen)` is false and the non-ASCII branch is taken. Its UTF-8 length is only 6, so the pre-check still passes at `outlen = 116`: `116 + 6 + 0 + 4 = 126 < 128`. The function therefore proceeds into punycode encoding even though the final ACE form plus terminator will need 13 bytes.

Root cause. After copying the `xn--` prefix for the final label, `outlen` becomes 120. This statement then sets `labellen = 8`, exposing all remaining bytes to `punycode_encode()` and leaving no reserved slot for the trailing `out[outlen] = 0`.

`punycode_encode()` emits the final label's 8-byte ACE tail `Do88-qrg` into bytes 120..127 of `lookupname`. Because `labellen` was allowed to consume all remaining space, `outlen` becomes exactly 128 after this increment.

Sink. There is no dot on the final label, so `outlen` is still 128 here and the terminator write targets `lookupname[128]`, one byte beyond the 0..127 stack array. This is the exact 1-byte ASan stack-buffer-overflow WRITE reported in the saved trace.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `docker exec gt-arvo_38985-workspace /bin/bash -lc /bin/arvo run`, which fed the staged `poc` to `/out/libpsl_load_fuzzer` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1` in `domain_to_punycode` with stack `psl_idna_toASCII -> add_punycode_if_needed -> psl_load_fp`.

format.name: public-suffix-list text rule
format.contract: The staged `poc` is the exact 62-byte single-line UTF-8 PSL-rule witness `ڸoa.Dڸ88.ڸoa.ڸ88.Dڸo8.ڸoa.Dڸ88.Dڸ888.Dڸ.Dڸo88.Dڸo88` with no trailing newline. The vulnerability-relevant contract is only what the saved bytes prove: the rule remains a non-comment, non-whitespace suffix entry short enough for `suffix_init()`, and its ACE expansion under the staged fallback punycode path exactly fills all 128 bytes of `lookupname` before the final terminator write. Source-grounded analysis does not generalize beyond that exact witness.
